newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA HARVESTS MORE WHEAT BY AUG 8 THAN YR-AGO.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA HARVESTS MORE WHEAT BY AUG 8 THAN YR-AGO.

text.p: Bulgaria had gathered one million tonnes more wheat from this year's crop by last weekend than at the same period last year, the agriculture ministry said on Tuesday.

"We have collected 2.95 million tonnes at an average yield of 3.16 tonnes per hectare by August 8 against 1.76 million tonnes at an average yield of 1.85 tonnes per hectare for the same period last year," a ministry spokeswoman told reporters.

Up to Tuesday Bulgaria had collected a total 3.14 million tonnes from 80 percent of the sown area, boosting the average yield to 3.2 tonnes per hectare despite heavy rains which had delayed the harvest, ministry figures show.
The wheat harvest deadline is end-July. Some 240,000 hectares have not been harvested so far and daily rainfall is affecting the quality of the crop.
Bulgaria's annual consumption is estimated at 1.6 million tonnes of bread wheat and 800,000 tonnes of feed wheat.
Agriculture minister Ventsislav Varbanov said on Monday private and state mills had bought a total of 800,000 tonnes of wheat so far.

The minimum purchase price was set at 230,000 levs per tonne for this year's crop in a bid to secure the country's grain balance after excessive wheat exports two years ago and a bad harvest in 1996 caused acute shortages earlier this year.

The State Fund for Reconstruction and Development said last week it had placed guarantees worth 203 billion levs out of a planned 230 billion levs with banks which extend credits to state companies to fund purchasing of wheat.
Bulgaria has to export some 232,000 tonnes of wheat this year under futures contracts agreed earlier this year. Poland has said it could accept cash payment for 100,000 tonnes of the total.
An export fee of 15 percent of international wheat prices has been also set in a bid to curb exports.
